title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property in Chinese Courts (2010)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the *Status of Intellectual Property Judicial Protection by Chinese Courts (2010)*

Fa [2011] No. 154

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In order to actively carry out the 2011 National Intellectual Property Publicity Week activities, thoroughly implement the national intellectual property strategy, further strengthen the promotion of intellectual property judicial protection, fully demonstrate the achievements of the people's courts in intellectual property judicial protection, and strive to create a favorable atmosphere conducive to the healthy development of the intellectual property judicial protection work of the people's courts, our Court has decided to publish the *Status of Intellectual Property Judicial Protection by Chinese Courts (2010)*.

The *Status of Intellectual Property Judicial Protection by Chinese Courts (2010)* comprehensively reviews and summarizes the intellectual property judicial protection work of the people's courts in 2010, fully demonstrates the achievements made in China's intellectual property judicial protection, and highlights China's determination and confidence in protecting intellectual property. People's courts at all levels across the country should take this opportunity to further enhance their understanding of the importance and urgency of strengthening intellectual property adjudication work, effectively play the leading role of judicial protection of intellectual property, innovate and work solidly, and strive to continuously create new prospects for intellectual property judicial protection work.

It is hereby notified.

April 12, 2011

Status of Intellectual Property Judicial Protection by Chinese Courts (2010)

Preface

In 2010, under the strong leadership of the Party and the effective supervision of the People's Congress, the people's courts held high the great banner of socialism with Chinese characteristics, guided by Deng Xiaoping Theory and the important thought of the "Three Represents," deeply implemented the Scientific Outlook on Development, strictly fulfilled the intellectual property adjudication duties conferred by the Constitution and laws, vigorously advanced the three key tasks of resolving social conflicts, innovating social management, and ensuring fair and honest law enforcement, actively served the overall situation, thoroughly implemented the national intellectual property strategy, fully exerted the leading role of judicial protection of intellectual property, continuously strengthened intellectual property judicial protection, and satisfactorily completed various intellectual property adjudication tasks, providing strong intellectual property judicial guarantees for accelerating the transformation of the economic development model, building an innovative country, and comprehensively building a moderately prosperous society.

In 2010, the intellectual property adjudication work of Chinese courts reached a new level.

I. Fulfilling Duties under the Constitution and Laws According to Law, New Progress in the Trial of Intellectual Property Cases

In 2010, the people's courts strictly performed their intellectual property adjudication duties according to law, always adhered to handling cases as the primary task, attached importance to studying the new characteristics of intellectual property cases, highlighted the focus of adjudication, innovated adjudication methods, strengthened supervision and guidance, concentrated efforts on trying cases, continuously improved the level of intellectual property case adjudication, and tried various types of intellectual property cases fairly and efficiently, further exerting the leading role of judicial protection of intellectual property.

Over the past year, the cases tried by the people's courts covered all areas of intellectual property law, and the functions of civil, administrative, and criminal adjudication were fully exercised. Intellectual property cases generally exhibited the following characteristics: the number of cases continued to increase, the number of new types of cases continued to increase, the number of major, complex, and difficult cases continued to increase, the number of foreign-related cases continued to increase, the difficulty of trial continued to increase, and the degree of social attention continued to increase.

The main channel role of intellectual property civil adjudication in intellectual property judicial protection continued to be exerted. In 2010, taking advantage of the implementation of the Tort Liability Law, the newly revised Patent Law and its judicial interpretations, the newly revised Copyright Law, and the Anti-Monopoly Law, the people's courts focused on promoting independent innovation capability and core competitiveness, strengthening patent protection; focused on promoting the formation of independent brands and the development of brand economy, strengthening trademark rights protection; focused on promoting the development of new business models and the prosperity of the cultural and creative industries, strengthening copyright protection; focused on improving market structure and maintaining fair competition, strengthening the adjudication of competition cases; and focused on creating a favorable trade and investment environment, strengthening equal protection. The number of intellectual property civil cases accepted by the people's courts continued to grow rapidly, and the main channel role of judicial resolution of intellectual property disputes became more apparent. Local courts across the country newly received and concluded 42,931 and 41,718 first-instance intellectual property civil cases, respectively, an increase of 40.18% and 36.74% over the previous year. The total amount of litigation标的 (subject matter) in newly received first-instance cases reached RMB 7,948,013,300. Among them, 5,785 patent cases were newly received, an increase of 30.82% over the previous year; 8,460 trademark cases, an increase of 22.50%; 24,719 copyright cases, an increase of 61.54%; 670 technology contract cases, a decrease of 10.31%; 1,131 competition cases (including 33 first-instance civil monopoly cases), a decrease of 11.78%; 12 discovery right and invention right disputes, an increase of 33.33%; 188 new plant variety cases, a decrease of 20.34%; and 1,966 other intellectual property cases, an increase of 14.17%. A total of 1,369 foreign-related first-instance intellectual property civil cases were concluded during the year, an increase of 0.59% over the previous year; 278 first-instance intellectual property civil cases involving Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan were concluded, a decrease of 21.25% year-on-year; and 23 first-instance civil monopoly cases were concluded. A total of 6,522 and 6,481 second-instance intellectual property civil cases were newly received and concluded, respectively, an increase of 22.13% and 18.01% year-on-year; 111 and 109 retrial cases were newly received and concluded, an increase of 11% and 1.87% year-on-year, respectively. The Supreme People's Court newly received and concluded 313 and 317 intellectual property civil cases, including 198 newly received cases for retrial application and 206 concluded (including those from previous years), effectively maintaining the uniformity of national intellectual property justice.

The quality and efficiency of intellectual property civil case adjudication continuously improved. The first-instance case conclusion rate of intellectual property civil cases in local courts across the country rose from 85.04% in 2009 to 86.39% in 2010; the appeal rate rose from 48.82% in 2009 to 49.65% in 2010; the retrial rate decreased from 0.33% in 2009 to 0.27% in 2010; and the rate of reversal of appealed cases or remand for retrial decreased from 6.00% in 2009 to 4.57% in 2010. The rate of first-instance intellectual property civil cases concluded within the trial period in local courts across the country rose from 97.38% in 2009 to 97.93% in 2010.

The unique role of pre-trial interim measures in protecting intellectual property rights was effectively exerted. In 2010, the people's courts accurately grasped the applicable conditions for pre-trial injunction and pre-trial property preservation, and lawfully and prudently rendered rulings to take measures. Local courts across the country prudently accepted a total of 55 applications for pre-trial preliminary injunctions related to intellectual property, with a support rate of 89.74%; accepted 294 applications for pre-trial evidence preservation, with a support rate of 97.46%. Attention was paid to actively taking evidence preservation measures according to law, effectively alleviating the burden of proof on the parties. 126 applications for pre-trial property preservation were accepted, with a support rate of 97.41%. For example, the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province used preliminary injunctions and other measures cautiously in intellectual property cases involving Taiwan, helping Taiwanese enterprises achieve a "soft landing," achieving the goal of "not affecting production, not affecting image, not affecting stability," which produced good social results.

Many cases tried by the people's courts not only involved complex specific issues of law application but also involved value judgments and judicial orientations in relevant economic, social, and cultural fields. These cases typically reflect the characteristics of current intellectual property cases, such as great influence, high difficulty in trial, disputes over law application, and high social attention. Examples include Eli Lilly and Company v. Jiangsu Hansoh Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (dispute over infringement of invention patent), Wang Qun v. France Pavilion of Shanghai World Expo (dispute over infringement of invention patent), Cheng Runchang v. Gong Judong et al. (dispute over infringement of utility model patent), Chen Jian v. Fushun Wanpu Printing Co., Ltd. (copyright dispute), Microsoft Corporation v. Dazhong Insurance Co., Ltd. (dispute over infringement of property rights in copyright), Lacoste S.A. (France) v. Crocodile International Pte Ltd (Singapore) et al. (dispute over infringement of exclusive right to use trademark), China Tianfu Cola Group Company (Chongqing) v. Chongqing Pepsi Tianfu Beverage Co., Ltd. et al. (dispute over infringement of technical secrets), Beijing Baidu Netcom Technology Co., Ltd. v. China United Network Communications Co., Ltd., Qingdao Branch et al. (unfair competition dispute), Lin Jinshan v. Fruit Tree Institute of Fujian Academy of Agricultural Sciences et al. (dispute over ownership of new plant variety rights), China Resources Siwei Technology Co., Ltd. v. Nanjing Yuanzhifeng Technology Co., Ltd. (dispute over infringement of exclusive right to integrated circuit layout design), etc.

The function of intellectual property administrative adjudication in supporting and supervising administrative authorities to act according to law was further strengthened. In 2010, the number of first-instance intellectual property administrative cases received and concluded increased significantly, mainly concentrated in trademark administrative cases. Local courts across the country newly received 2,590 first-instance intellectual property administrative cases, an increase of 25% year-on-year; concluded 2,391 cases, an increase of 21.31% year-on-year. Among them, 551 patent cases were newly received, a decrease of 17.51% year-on-year; 2,026 trademark cases, an increase of 47.23%; 2 copyright cases, a decrease of 50%; and 11 other cases. The Supreme People's Court newly received and concluded 60 and 56 intellectual property administrative cases. The main reasons for the increase in trademark administrative cases were the significant increase in cases reviewed by the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board, the increase in litigation rate of reviewed cases, and the concentrated clearance of backlogged cases by the Board. Among the concluded cases, 1,776 were affirmed (74.28%); 330 were overturned (13.80%); 162 were withdrawn (6.78%); 87 claims were dismissed (3.64%); 30 were dismissed for lack of standing; 4 were transferred; and 1 case was concluded in other ways.

First-instance intellectual property administrative cases involving foreign, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan elements increased significantly, totaling 1,004 cases, accounting for 41.99% of concluded first-instance intellectual property administrative cases. Among them, 815 foreign-related first-instance intellectual property administrative cases were concluded, 98 cases involving Hong Kong, 11 cases involving Macao, and 80 cases involving Taiwan.

Second-instance intellectual property administrative cases increased significantly. Courts across the country newly received 394 second-instance intellectual property administrative cases and concluded 240, including 206 affirming the original judgment, 20 reversing, 1 remanding for retrial, 9 withdrawing, and 4 dismissing appeals. Cases with significant social impact include Honda Motor Co., Ltd. (Japan) v. Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office and Shijiazhuang Shuanghuan Automobile Co., Ltd. (administrative dispute over invalidation of design patent), Shanxi Xinghuacun Fenjiu Factory Co., Ltd. v. Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce and Third Party: Anhui Xinghuacun Group Co., Ltd. (administrative dispute over trademark opposition review regarding the "Xinghuacun" trademark), etc.

The function of intellectual property criminal adjudication in punishing and deterring crime was further exerted. In 2010, the number of first-instance intellectual property criminal cases increased significantly. Courts across the country newly received 3,992 first-instance cases, an increase of 9.58% year-on-year. Among them, 1,294 were crimes of infringing intellectual property rights (including 1,153 cases of counterfeiting registered trademarks, etc.), an increase of 26.99%; 596 were cases of crimes of producing and selling counterfeit and shoddy goods involving intellectual property infringement, a decrease of 6.73%; 2,078 were cases of crimes of illegal business operations involving intellectual property infringement, an increase of 6.62%; and 24 were other cases.

Courts across the country concluded a total of 3,942 first-instance criminal cases involving intellectual property infringement, an increase of 7.7% year-on-year; 6,001 persons were subject to effective judgments, including 6,000 persons convicted. Among the concluded cases, 1,254 cases were adjudicated as crimes of infringing intellectual property rights, with 1,966 persons subject to effective judgments, an increase of 24.53% and 22.49% year-on-year respectively; 609 cases were adjudicated as crimes of producing and selling counterfeit and shoddy goods (involving intellectual property infringement), with 926 persons subject to effective judgments; 2,054 cases were adjudicated as crimes of illegal business operations (involving intellectual property infringement), with 3,068 persons subject to effective judgments; and 25 cases involving intellectual property infringement were adjudicated under other crimes, with 41 persons subject to effective judgments. Among the cases adjudicated as crimes of infringing intellectual property rights, 585 cases were adjudicated as the crime of counterfeiting a registered trademark, with 1,028 persons subject to effective judgments; 345 cases as the crime of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark, with 459 persons subject to effective judgments; 182 cases as the crime of illegally manufacturing or selling illegally manufactured representations of a registered trademark, with 253 persons subject to effective judgments; 2 cases as the crime of counterfeiting a patent, with 3 persons subject to effective judgments; 85 cases as the crime of infringing copyright, with 142 persons subject to effective judgments; 5 cases as the crime of selling infringing reproductions, with 10 persons subject to effective judgments; and 50 cases as the crime of infringing trade secrets, with 71 persons subject to effective judgments. Among these, the case of Liu Zhaolong for counterfeiting a registered trademark attracted widespread public attention.

Strengthening case mediation, focusing on conflict resolution. The people's courts conscientiously implemented the *Several Opinions on Further Implementing the Work Principle of "Mediation Priority, Combination of Mediation and Adjudication"* issued by the Supreme People's Court. In case adjudication, they adhered to the principle of legality and voluntariness, and for cases that could be mediated according to law, that were suitable for mediation based on the facts, and where mediation would produce better results, they first chose mediation to resolve the dispute. They paid attention to standardizing mediation work, correctly handling the relationship between mediation and adjudication, and promptly rendered judgments according to law for cases unsuitable for mediation or where mediation failed. They insisted on making efforts to expand the field of mediation, standardize judicial mediation procedures, focus on mediation quality, and improve mediation efficiency.

In 2010, the mediation work of intellectual property litigation in the people's courts developed toward institutionalization, standardization, and rationalization, and reached a new level. The average rate of mediation and withdrawal of first-instance intellectual property civil cases nationwide reached 66.76%, an increase of 5.68 percentage points year-on-year. The Supreme People's Court successfully mediated or had 24 difficult intellectual property cases withdrawn. For example, Bayer CropScience S.A. (France) v. Anhui Huaxing Chemical Industry Co., Ltd. (foreign-related patent infringement case), Xi'an Qiangsheng Company v. Shanghai Qiangsheng Company (trademark infringement dispute), etc. The successful mediation of these cases not only satisfied the parties but also produced very positive social responses. Higher People's Courts in Shanghai, Tianjin, and other places issued guiding opinions on further strengthening the mediation of intellectual property civil disputes. Higher People's Courts in Guangdong, Hebei, Sichuan, Henan, Guangxi, Guizhou, etc., as well as the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court and the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province, continuously explored and summarized a complete set of standardized mediation methods.

Promoting fairness through openness, winning public trust through fairness. The people's courts adhered to "sunshine justice," ensuring fairness through openness. They further clarified the contents, procedures, and methods that must be open in six aspects: case filing, trial, execution, hearings, documents, and judicial affairs. They creatively improved the transparency of intellectual property adjudication through press conference systems, court open day activities, live webcasts, and other methods, promoted the fairness of intellectual property adjudication, standardized the exercise of judicial discretion in intellectual property, and won the credibility of intellectual property justice, truly achieving "sunshine justice." On the "12.4" public open day, the Supreme People's Court for the first time selected an intellectual property case trial for public observation. The court system of Hunan Province established a long-term mechanism for representatives of the People's Congress to observe trials and live webcasts of trials, regularly inviting representatives of the People's Congress to observe intellectual property case trials. The court system of Liaoning Province generally equipped intellectual property trial courts with a high degree of informatization and intelligence, and normalized the management of live webcasts of trials. Higher People's Courts in Fujian, Yunnan, etc., and Intermediate People's Courts in Fuzhou, Kunming, etc., used live webcasts to enable a broader public to timely understand the trial proceedings of intellectual property cases.

Initiating the white paper system on intellectual property protection, comprehensively demonstrating the intellectual property judicial adjudication work of the people's courts. In April 2010, the Supreme People's Court for the first time published the white paper *Status of Intellectual Property Judicial Protection by Chinese Courts (2009)* (in Chinese and English). While briefly introducing the work of intellectual property judicial protection since the reform and opening up over 30 years, it comprehensively reviewed and summarized the intellectual property judicial protection work of the people's courts in 2009, fully demonstrated the achievements of intellectual property judicial protection by Chinese courts, and highlighted China's determination and confidence in protecting intellectual property. This was the first time the Supreme People's Court publicly and comprehensively introduced the status of intellectual property judicial protection by the people's courts to domestic and foreign audiences in the form of a white paper, and it was an important measure for the people's courts to further implement the national intellectual property strategy and strengthen intellectual property judicial protection. Higher People's Courts in Tianjin, Chongqing, Shandong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Gansu, Hebei, etc., published white papers on intellectual property protection for 2009. The Higher People's Court of Jiangsu Province published a blue paper on intellectual property judicial protection for 2009. The publication of these white papers (blue papers) provided a comprehensive and systematic introduction to the status of intellectual property adjudication in the respective regions, allowing the whole society to understand intellectual property adjudication, accept social inspection and supervision, and ensure the fairness and justice of intellectual property justice.

While continuing to operate the "China Intellectual Property Judgments and Decisions Online," the Supreme People's Court officially launched the "sub-website for Intellectual Property Judicial Protection" on its official website. These two websites became authoritative information release platforms for the achievements of intellectual property judicial protection by the people's courts. Through these two websites, the public can timely learn and grasp the dynamics and information of intellectual property judicial protection by the people's courts. As of the end of 2010, 41,696 effective intellectual property judgments and decisions had been made public through the "China Intellectual Property Judgments and Decisions Online." Local courts continued to publicly disclose various types of intellectual property adjudication work information in a timely manner through local court websites.

II. Focusing on the Intellectual Property Judicial Needs of Economic and Social Development, New Breakthroughs in Implementing the National Intellectual Property Strategy

In 2010, the people's courts always adhered to the concept of active justice, identified the entry point for intellectual property adjudication work to serve the overall situation of economic and social development, closely focused on the national strategic deployment to accelerate the transformation of the economic development model and maintain stable and relatively fast economic development, continued to deeply implement the national intellectual property strategy, and provided strong intellectual property judicial guarantees for promoting sound and rapid economic and social development.

Adhering to the concept of active judicial protection of intellectual property rights, we actively serve the overall domestic and international landscape. After the 17th National Congress of the Communist Party of China proposed the major strategic task of accelerating the transformation of the economic development model, in July 2010, the Supreme People's Court issued Several Opinions on Providing Judicial Guarantees and Services for Accelerating the Transformation of the Economic Development Model. These Opinions clearly stated that all types of intellectual property cases should be properly adjudicated to safeguard and serve the promotion of independent innovation, strengthen judicial protection of intellectual property in key areas, promote the development of strategic industries, facilitate the formation of independent brands and the development of the brand economy, maintain the core competitiveness of enterprises, uphold fair competition in the market order, promote cultural innovation, and flourish the cultural market.

In February 2010, to actively respond to the new situations and challenges in intellectual property adjudication in the post-international financial crisis period, the Supreme People's Court organized a "Seminar on Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property in the Post-International Financial Crisis Period" to study in depth how to fully utilize the functions of intellectual property adjudication to mitigate and resolve the adverse impacts of the international financial crisis on China's economy and society. In April, to implement the Party Central Committee's decisions and deployments on advancing the three key tasks and the spirit of the National Conference of Presidents of Higher People's Courts, the Supreme People's Court held a National Forum on Intellectual Property Adjudication Work in Luoyang, Henan Province, to seriously study and deploy intellectual property adjudication work under the new circumstances, clarifying the main tasks and work measures. After the forum, higher people's courts nationwide, in conjunction with local work realities, promptly convened meetings to deploy and implement the forum's spirit.

To ensure the smooth progress of major national events such as the Shanghai World Expo, the Guangzhou Asian Games, and the Asian Para Games, the people's courts proactively provided intellectual property judicial guarantees and services for these events. The Supreme People's Court formed a special research team to visit the Shanghai Higher People's Court and the Shanghai World Expo Coordination Bureau to investigate issues regarding the judicial protection of World Expo intellectual property, guiding relevant local courts to properly adjudicate related intellectual property cases. The Shanghai Higher People's Court issued special guiding opinions on the application of law in adjudicating intellectual property cases involving the World Expo, clarifying the legal application standards for World Expo-related intellectual property disputes, and formulated a work plan for intellectual property adjudication services and guarantees for the World Expo. The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court held a symposium on strengthening the protection of Asian Games intellectual property rights with the Asian Games Organizing Committee and its legal advisors, comprehensively understanding the judicial needs for Asian Games intellectual property protection, and put forward judicial suggestions for strengthening such protection.

The people's courts actively responded to the State Council's special campaign to "Crack Down on Intellectual Property Infringement and the Production and Sale of Counterfeit and Shoddy Goods," intensifying efforts to combat crimes of intellectual property infringement. They strengthened cooperation with procuratorial, public security, industrial and commercial, copyright, and customs authorities to form a joint force, collectively promoting the sound and rapid development of China's intellectual property undertakings. They actively carried out judicial suggestion work on intellectual property matters, providing references for other departments to better implement the National Intellectual Property Strategy. For example, higher people's courts in Shandong, Hunan, and other places issued judicial suggestions on notarized preservation of evidence in an online environment. The Guangdong Higher People's Court, in its trials, discovered that some foreign enterprises were using intellectual property as a commercial tool to suppress and curb competitors in China, and issued judicial suggestions to relevant units, proposing that an intellectual property early warning mechanism be established, along with a foreign-related response and rights protection assistance mechanism for intellectual property. The Shandong Higher People's Court put forward specific opinions on how intellectual property adjudication work should guarantee and serve the transformation of the economic development model, clarifying the positioning and key areas of intellectual property judicial protection. The Sichuan Higher People's Court issued special opinions to guide the province's intellectual property judicial work to closely focus on accelerating the transformation of the economic development model.

Actively promoting judicial reform in the intellectual property field, the intellectual property adjudication system and working mechanisms were further improved. The people's courts continuously strengthened awareness of intellectual property judicial reform, continued to focus on implementing the National Intellectual Property Strategy concerning the work of the people's courts, actively promoted reform and improvement of the intellectual property adjudication system and working mechanisms, and further optimized the intellectual property adjudication system.

The pilot work of having the intellectual property adjudication tribunals of the people's courts uniformly accept intellectual property civil, administrative, and criminal cases (i.e., "three-in-one") was steadily advanced. In July 2010, the Supreme People's Court held a "Symposium on the Pilot Work of Centralized Adjudication of Intellectual Property Civil, Administrative, and Criminal Cases by Intellectual Property Adjudication Tribunals" in Kunshan City, Jiangsu Province, attended by representatives from relevant central departments and some courts conducting the "three-in-one" pilot. The Supreme People's Court newly approved the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court, Xiamen Intermediate People's Court, the two-level people's courts of Shenzhen, Foshan, and Zhongshan, as well as the Gulou District People's Court of Fuzhou and the Siming District People's Court of Xiamen, to carry out the "three-in-one" pilot. As of the end of December 2010, five higher people's courts, 49 intermediate people's courts, and 42 basic people's courts nationwide had conducted relevant pilots.

Continuing to improve the jurisdictional layout of intellectual property cases and further optimize the allocation of adjudication resources. In January 2010, the Supreme People's Court issued the Notice on Adjusting the Standards for Local People's Courts at All Levels to Accept First-Instance Intellectual Property Civil Cases and the Notice on Issuing the Standards for Basic People's Courts to Accept First-Instance Intellectual Property Civil Cases, comprehensively adjusting and uniformly clarifying the standards for intellectual property civil case jurisdiction at all levels. While strictly controlling the jurisdiction courts for technology-related cases and well-known trademark cases, appropriately increasing the number of basic people's courts with jurisdiction over general intellectual property cases, encouraging intermediate and basic courts to implement cross-regional centralized jurisdiction, and exploring the designation of some basic people's courts to accept certain patent cases. The Supreme People's Court approved the Kunshan City People's Court in Jiangsu Province to conduct a pilot for adjudicating utility model and design patent dispute cases. Thus, two basic people's courts had carried out pilot work for adjudicating utility model and design patent dispute cases. As of the end of December 2010, the number of intermediate people's courts with jurisdiction over patent, new plant variety, integrated circuit layout design, and cases involving well-known trademark determination was 76, 44, 46, and 41 respectively, and the number of basic people's courts with jurisdiction over general intellectual property cases reached 101.

Relevant local courts, in accordance with the spirit of judicial reform and in conjunction with local realities, formulated detailed plans to effectively implement the "three-in-one" pilot work for civil, administrative, and criminal cases, as well as adjudication work. For example, higher people's courts in Zhejiang, Inner Mongolia, and other places strengthened coordination with the procuratorates and public security departments, issuing relevant guiding opinions on criminal judicial protection issues in the "three-in-one" pilot work of intellectual property adjudication to ensure the smooth progress of the pilot.

Strengthening innovation in the intellectual property adjudication system, striving to improve the level of intellectual property justice. Given the technical and specialized nature of intellectual property cases, the Supreme People's Court has always attached importance to establishing and improving litigation systems such as judicial appraisal, expert witnesses, and technical investigation, while encouraging and guiding capable courts to actively explore effective methods and specific practices of technical investigation in adjudicating technical cases such as patents.

In April 2010, the Supreme People's Court and the China Association for Science and Technology jointly signed a Memorandum of Cooperation on Intellectual Property Judicial Protection, providing a long-term and stable operational platform for strengthening cooperation between the Supreme People's Court and the China Association for Science and Technology in the field of intellectual property judicial protection. An expert database of specially invited science and technology consultants for the Supreme People's Court was established. Eleven academicians of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the Chinese Academy of Engineering, including Yuan Longping and Zhong Nanshan, were appointed as science and technology consultants for the Supreme People's Court. The Supreme People's Court emphasized the role of science and technology experts in providing macro policy advice on intellectual property judicial protection, offering intellectual support on technical issues in cases, and coordinating the resolution of intellectual property disputes. As a major measure to vigorously promote the reform of intellectual property adjudication, this marked a new step for the people's courts in improving the intellectual property dispute resolution mechanism and raising the level of intellectual property judicial protection. Higher people's courts in Shanghai, Jiangsu, Qinghai, Hebei, Zhejiang, Guangxi, Shanxi, and other places actively explored the establishment and improvement of mechanisms to ascertain technical facts in cases, set up expert consultation databases, and piloted expert juror and expert witness systems. These mechanisms and systems played an important role in solving specialized technical problems and improved the quality of intellectual property case adjudication. The Xiamen Intermediate People's Court attempted to establish a confidentiality order system for intellectual property cases, which better resolved the issue of trade secret protection during litigation, alleviating the concerns of rights holders in seeking judicial relief.

Intensifying the promotion of intellectual property judicial protection, building the "4.26" World Intellectual Property Day Promotion Week platform. Taking the "4.26" World Intellectual Property Day as an opportunity, the people's courts made efforts to build the "4.26" World Intellectual Property Day Promotion Week platform, adopting feasible methods to widely publicize the achievements of China's intellectual property judicial protection from multiple perspectives, fully showcasing the demeanor of intellectual property judges, and striving to establish a positive image of China's intellectual property judicial protection. During the "4.26" World Intellectual Property Day Promotion Week in 2010, the Supreme People's Court held a press conference, releasing the White Paper on the Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property in Chinese Courts (2009) (in Chinese and English), the Top 10 Cases and 50 Typical Cases of Intellectual Property Judicial Protection in Chinese Courts in 2009, the Annual Report of the Supreme People's Court on Intellectual Property Cases (2009), and important intellectual property judicial documents such as the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Administrative Cases Involving Trademark Authorization and Confirmation, and jointly signed the Memorandum of Cooperation on Intellectual Property Judicial Protection with the China Association for Science and Technology. Local courts nationwide, in accordance with the requirements of the Supreme People's Court, also made great efforts in the breadth and depth of publicity, paying attention to both content and form, emphasizing the role of traditional publicity methods while utilizing new ones, leveraging the influence of central media as well as local and foreign media. They made full use of newspapers, television stations, radio stations, broadcast, websites, books, periodicals, slogans, and other platforms, organizing judges to vigorously publicize the significance of intellectual property judicial protection, judicial policies, and new achievements, which played a positive role in raising the public's awareness of intellectual property. The court system in Jiangsu Province successfully held the Commemorative Conference for the 15th Anniversary of Specialized Intellectual Property Adjudication and a Seminar on Intellectual Property Protection and Interest Balance, publishing "Innovation and Development: A Collection of Achievements of 15 Years of Intellectual Property Adjudication in Jiangsu Courts" and "A Glorious Journey, a Beautiful Future: A Commemorative Album." The Zhejiang Higher People's Court held an intellectual property press conference, answering questions from journalists from 40 domestic and foreign media outlets. The Hubei Higher People's Court cooperated with the media "Science, Technology and Law" to open a column on judicial protection of intellectual property. The Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps Branch distributed 6,000 intellectual property knowledge questionnaires and displayed over 60 exhibition boards during the event. Courts in Hainan, Tibet, and other places also adopted various methods to widely publicize the achievements of the people's courts in intellectual property protection.

Strengthening international exchanges and cooperation on intellectual property, enhancing the international influence of China's intellectual property judicial protection. In 2010, against the backdrop of accelerating international economic integration and the internationalization of the international intellectual property protection system, the people's courts firmly adopted an international perspective, strengthened international exchanges and cooperation on intellectual property, continuously improved the level of intellectual property adjudication, and focused on enhancing the positive international image of China's intellectual property judicial protection. Through foreign affairs activities, they actively responded to the concerns of foreign parties, clarified misunderstandings, promoted China's achievements in intellectual property protection, and maintained the international image. The Supreme People's Court sent personnel to participate in the China-EU Intellectual Property Working Group Meeting, the Intellectual Property Working Group Meeting of the U.S.-China Joint Commission on Commerce and Trade, and the China-Switzerland Intellectual Property Working Group Meeting, actively participated in the activities of Phase II of the China-EU Intellectual Property Project, comprehensively demonstrating China's achievements in intellectual property protection, expressing China's position and determination on intellectual property judicial protection, and safeguarding national interests. The people's courts continued to strengthen intellectual property exchanges and cooperation in the economic and trade field through dialogues and specialized intellectual property working group mechanisms with the United States, the European Union, Switzerland, Russia, Japan, and Brazil, as well as through channels such as the Japan-China Joint Intellectual Property Delegation. Intellectual property judges from the Supreme People's Court hosted nearly 100 visits from high-level delegations from Japan, the United States, and other countries. At the same time, they organized outstanding judges from the national court system to conduct study tours to the United States, Japan, Europe, and other countries based on work needs, and selected judges to undergo training and exchanges in these countries. The Zhejiang Higher People's Court received members of the American Intellectual Property Law Association and judges from the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, engaging in in-depth exchanges on intellectual property judicial protection of mutual interest.

III. Unifying the Standards for the Application of Intellectual Property Laws, with New Progress in Trial Supervision and Professional Guidance

Uniformity in the application of law is an inherent requirement of equality before the law, an inevitable manifestation of judicial fairness and authority, and a fundamental characteristic of a country governed by the rule of law. In 2010, the people's courts consistently attached great importance to the uniformity of intellectual property law application, identified prominent issues affecting the fairness of judgments and the uniformity of judicial standards, continuously innovated and strengthened trial management, further improved the working mechanisms and systems for trial supervision and professional guidance, and effectively safeguarded the fairness and uniformity of intellectual property justice.

Strengthening the macro-level policy regulation of intellectual property justice, standardizing the exercise of discretionary power in intellectual property adjudication. The Supreme People's Court, based on the different characteristics and protection needs of various types of intellectual property, clarified macro-level judicial policies of classification, differentiated treatment, and appropriate leniency and severity, further clarified and refined the judicial policies for intellectual property cases, and ensured the implementation and enforcement of these policies through various means, effectively playing the macro-regulatory role of judicial policies and promoting the standardization and uniformity of intellectual property adjudication work.

In April 2010, the Supreme People's Court issued the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Administrative Cases Involving Trademark Authorization and Confirmation. This was the first time the Supreme People's Court used a normative document to provide guiding opinions on several judicial review standards for administrative cases involving trademark authorization and confirmation. These Opinions clarified relevant legal boundaries, unified judicial standards, and were of great significance for the people's courts to correctly fulfill their judicial review duties and regulate trademark authorization and confirmation actions. In November of the same year, the Supreme People's Court issued the Notice on Doing a Good Job in the Adjudication of Copyright Dispute Cases Involving Internet Cafes. This Notice, targeting prominent issues in copyright dispute cases involving Internet cafes, promptly clarified the trial principles and specific standards for such cases, playing an important role in protecting the copyright of parties according to law, effectively curbing infringement, promoting information dissemination and standardizing the dissemination order, and promoting the healthy development of related Internet cultural industries.

Actively exploring the case guidance system for intellectual property, promptly publishing typical intellectual property cases. The people's courts have always attached great importance to the exemplary role of typical cases in intellectual property adjudication, making the selection and promotion of typical cases an important task, and striving to strengthen the standardization, institutionalization, and long-term effect of case guidance work. In April 2010, the Supreme People's Court published the Annual Report of the Supreme People's Court on Intellectual Property Cases (2009). Based on a systematic review of typical intellectual property cases with final conclusions adjudicated by the Supreme People's Court in 2009, 37 typical cases were selected, summarizing 44 typical issues of law application clarified in the judgments of these typical cases, and publicly released to the society in the form of an annual report. Issuing the annual report is a centralized display of the typical cases adjudicated by the Supreme People's Court itself, an exploration and attempt to innovate the mode of trial guidance, and a major measure to promote judicial openness and accept supervision from all sectors. The release of the Top 10 Cases and 50 Typical Cases of Intellectual Property Judicial Protection in National Courts in 2009 fully utilized the exemplary effect of cases. The Top 10 Cases and 50 Typical Cases covered the three major litigation areas of intellectual property civil, administrative, and criminal cases, including almost all types of intellectual property cases such as patents, new plant varieties, copyrights, trademarks, and unfair competition. These typical cases vividly demonstrated to the society the functional role of the people's courts in strengthening intellectual property judicial protection, safeguarding the legitimate interests of rights holders, and reasonably defining the scope of rights, helping to raise the public's awareness of the rule of law in intellectual property, and promoting the formation of a culture of independent innovation and honest and law-abiding competition. Local courts nationwide selected local typical intellectual property cases and excellent cases through various forms. Higher people's courts in Tianjin, Chongqing, Shandong, Anhui, Fujian, Hunan, Sichuan, Heilongjiang, and other places published their local top ten typical cases. The Higher People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region established a typical case guidance system. The Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province published classic cases of intellectual property judicial protection.

Strengthen special research on intellectual property adjudication, and focus on improving the quality of judicial interpretations and judicial interpretive documents of intellectual property. The people's courts have firmly established the concept of "promoting adjudication through research," attached great importance to research work on intellectual property adjudication, and laid a solid foundation for issuing high-quality judicial interpretations and judicial interpretive documents. Research levels have been continuously enhanced through various forms such as holding specialized seminars, inviting experts to give lectures, organizing judge forums, conducting field investigations, writing research reports, and publishing books, with an emphasis on transforming results. In 2010, the Supreme People's Court organized relevant courts nationwide to carry out extensive targeted special research activities, promptly and effectively studied and resolved prominent issues arising in judicial practice, and strengthened investigation and research on the application of law in new types of cases. The focus was on multiple research projects including judicial protection of copyright in the network environment, trial standards for patent grant and confirmation cases, research on trademark grant and confirmation cases, copyright protection of foreign works without administrative licensing, copyright infringement issues in internet cafes, judicial protection of trade secrets, research on the judicial protection system for intellectual property during the "12th Five-Year Plan" period, legal issues in adjudicating civil monopoly disputes, legal application issues in administrative adjudication of intellectual property, and issues related to exploring the establishment of an appellate court for intellectual property. Through research activities, the judicial status and dynamics in the intellectual property field were fully understood and grasped, resulting in rich research outcomes. Based on sufficient and mature research, judicial interpretations and judicial interpretive documents on intellectual property were issued in a timely manner. Among them, specialized trial guidance opinions were promptly proposed on the basis of research regarding copyright protection of foreign works without administrative licensing, copyright infringement issues in internet cafes, and trial standards for trademark grant and confirmation cases. Courts at various levels also produced a number of research outcomes with trial guidance value. After years of cultivation, emphasizing research and strengthening learning have become professional qualities of intellectual property judges. The Professional Committee of Intellectual Property Adjudication Theory, together with other departments, co-hosted the "Symposium on the 20th Anniversary of the Promulgation of the Copyright Law and Basic Theories of Copyright Protection" and edited and published the "Research on China's Intellectual Property Adjudication Theory" (Volume 2). The Beijing High People's Court published three monographs: "Classic Cases of Intellectual Property" (Volumes 5 and 6) and "Classic Cases of Network Copyright."

Broaden the channels for business guidance on intellectual property adjudication, and effectively fulfill the duty of business guidance on intellectual property adjudication. In 2010, higher-level people's courts continuously broadened the channels for business guidance on intellectual property adjudication. By formulating judicial interpretations, issuing judicial documents, issuing guiding opinions, conducting special research, holding professional meetings, carrying out targeted training, establishing internal publications, and publishing guiding cases, they effectively assumed the responsibility of providing business guidance on intellectual property adjudication to lower-level people's courts, unified the judicial adjudication standards for intellectual property, standardized the exercise of judicial discretion in intellectual property, and ensured judicial fairness in intellectual property. The Supreme People's Court summarized the trial experience of cases for retrial applications, summarized issues arising in trials across courts nationwide, and strengthened targeted guidance for lower-level courts on key issues. It studied and coordinated similar cases to guide relevant courts in correctly applying the law. It carried out special regulation on the judicial recognition of well-known trademarks, deeply conducted reviews of cases recognizing well-known trademarks, and judicial protection of well-known trademarks entered a standardized track. The Shanghai High People's Court formulated guiding judicial documents on applying statutory damages to determine the amount of compensation in intellectual property infringement disputes, clarifying several basic principles for applying statutory damages. The Jilin High People's Court organized outstanding intellectual property adjudication judges to conduct circuit lectures to various intermediate people's courts in the province. High people's courts in Hunan, Ningxia, and other places established coordination and resolution mechanisms for series of cases. The Shanxi High People's Court established and improved the contact and reporting system between higher and lower-level courts. The Tianjin High People's Court edited the "Chronicle of Major Events in Tianjin Intellectual Property Adjudication (2005-2009)" and "Tianjin Court Intellectual Property Adjudication." High people's courts in Heilongjiang, Shanxi, Gansu, and other places compiled books on intellectual property adjudication guidance.

IV. Strengthen the team building of intellectual property judges, with new improvement in the overall quality of the intellectual property judge team

Team building has always been the foundation of the people's courts' work. In 2010, the people's courts closely integrated the actual work of intellectual property adjudication, innovated and strengthened trial management, strengthened the team building of intellectual property judges, deeply carried out the thematic practice activity of "people's judges for the people," vigorously cultivated the core judicial values of "fairness, integrity, and serving the people" among intellectual property judges, and strived to build a high-quality team of intellectual property judges who are politically steadfast, professionally competent, dedicated to the people, and fair and incorruptible.

Always focus on improving the judicial capacity for intellectual property. Continuously improving the judicial capacity of the judge team is an inevitable requirement for ensuring social fairness and justice. In 2010, the people's courts, as always, treated professional learning and training as important tasks to enhance the judicial capacity of the intellectual property judge team and grasped them firmly and effectively. Emphasis was placed on improving judges' professional knowledge and trial skills, deeply carrying out the construction of learning-oriented trial divisions, strengthening trial management, perfecting and improving learning and training systems, and focusing on cultivating a number of professional and expert judges. The basic-level infrastructure, especially the basic-level construction of intellectual property adjudication in grassroots courts, was effectively grasped as an urgent task. In professional training, in addition to measures taken by the Supreme People's Court such as holding seminar conferences and training courses, higher and intermediate people's courts also assumed the responsibility of professional training, innovated methods for cultivating professional judges, enhanced the pertinence and effectiveness of professional training, and strengthened trial guidance through various forms such as centralized training, upper-lower counterpart exchanges, court observation, and case review. Intellectual property judges continuously strengthened self-learning, not only focusing on learning new knowledge of intellectual property laws, judicial documents of higher-level courts, and judgments in typical cases, but also focusing on learning basic scientific and technological knowledge. Many courts, especially those with heavy caseloads, paid attention to incorporating personnel with backgrounds in science and engineering into the intellectual property adjudication team. The Supreme People's Court held two national training courses on intellectual property adjudication practice at the National Judges College, with nearly 200 intellectual property judges participating in the training. Many courts organized various forms of selection activities for post pacesetters and case-handling experts. Courts in central and western regions such as Jiangxi and Qinghai organized judges to observe and study, or follow shifts, in eastern developed regions. High people's courts in Shanghai, Hunan, Guangdong, and other places established long-term exchange mechanisms for personnel with specialized intellectual property institutions such as the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office. High people's courts in Chongqing, Shandong, Guangdong, Hebei, Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia, Guangxi, Liaoning, and other provinces strengthened training for judges through various forms.

Always focus on improving the judicial work style in intellectual property. Work style is image, and work style is credibility. In 2010, the people's courts continued to deepen the construction of judicial work style, carried out education on mass viewpoints, established the tenet of justice for the people, enhanced the mass concept and awareness of intellectual property judges, and maintained an excellent work style. They organized intellectual property judges to carry out activities such as entering communities, enterprises, schools, and groups, fully listened to opinions and suggestions from intellectual circles, emerging industrial circles, business circles, social groups, and the people on improving judicial protection of intellectual property, and strengthened ties with the people. High people's courts in Shandong, Jiangsu, Liaoning, Sichuan, Inner Mongolia, Guizhou, Heilongjiang, and other provinces strengthened their connection with enterprises, understood the development situation of industries, and raised enterprises' awareness of protecting their own intellectual property rights. The Pingxiang Intermediate People's Court in Jiangxi Province established an intellectual property assistance center to provide free consultation, advice, and other services to enterprises, institutions, and individuals. The Heping District People's Court in Tianjin established a circuit court within the Heping District No. 6 Courtyard Cultural and Creative Industry Park. The vast number of intellectual property judges strived to establish the core judicial values of fairness, integrity, and serving the people, continuously improved their own professional ethics, and effectively implemented the "Basic Standards for Judges' Professional Ethics," "Codes of Conduct for Judges," and "Basic Standards for Civilized Language Used by People's Courts" promulgated by the Supreme People's Court. They gave full play to the exemplary role of advanced models, deeply studied the advanced models such as "Good Judge Trusted by the Masses" Chen Yanping and "Pioneer of the Times" and National Excellent Judge Long Jinpin. The Intellectual Property Tribunal of the Beijing High People's Court was awarded the "WIPO Copyright Gold Medal" by the World Intellectual Property Organization. The Intellectual Property Adjudication Tribunal of the Shanghai High People's Court was awarded the title of "Advanced Collective for Special Actions on Intellectual Property Protection at the World Expo."

Always focus on promoting judicial integrity in intellectual property. Judicial integrity is the professional ethics guarantee for judicial fairness and concerns the success or failure of the people's judicial cause. In 2010, the people's courts continued to strengthen the construction of clean government within the intellectual property judge team, emphasizing both institutional supervision and moral constraints. They further strengthened judicial integrity education, adopted more effective forms to avoid mechanical preaching, concentrated on carrying out warning education, and enhanced the awareness of resisting corruption and preventing degradation. They strictly implemented the "Five Prohibitions" and various anti-corruption systems, and eradicated the soil breeding corruption. The Supreme People's Court guided local people's courts at all levels to further enhance the awareness of consciously accepting supervision, strengthened supervision and restriction, actively improved the supervision and restriction mechanism, strived to promote judicial fairness and integrity, and continuously improved judicial credibility.

Closing Remarks

2011 is the first year of the implementation of the national "12th Five-Year Plan." The people's courts will firmly seize the important strategic development opportunities for the cause of judicial protection of intellectual property while facing challenges. The people's courts will always be guided by Deng Xiaoping Theory and the important thought of "Three Represents," firmly grasp the theme of scientific development, closely follow the main line of accelerating the transformation of the economic development mode, highlight the focus of handling cases and enforcing laws, strengthen the foundation of team building, continue to deeply advance three key tasks, exercise independent and impartial intellectual property adjudication power according to law, deeply carry out the thematic education and practice activity of "Carry forward traditions, strengthen convictions, enforce the law for the people," strive to push the cause of intellectual property adjudication to a new level, and provide more powerful judicial guarantees for promoting independent innovation capabilities and enhancing the core competitiveness of the country!
